title: Fourth reason: the legal covenant demanded flawless obedience—any lightest fault lost life and incurred curse
source_text: LXVII. Praeterea Deus cum homine integro foedus legale pangens ab eo exigebat obedientiam undequaque perfectam, & omnibus suis numeris absolutam, tanquam conditionem sine qua non poterat vitam aeternam & beatam assequi, & maledictionem divinam effugere. Jam autem perfectio illa, quam lex in rigore suo, & prout primum fuit homini lata postulat, excludit omne peccatum, etiam levissimum. Ac proinde quolibet peccato etiam levissimo, homo integer poterat vita aeterna excidere, & ma-ledictionem divinam incurrere. Unde manifesto sequitur omne peccatum, quantum-libet leve, esse natura sua mortale, non veniale. Quod vero sub foedere legali, homo integer quolibet peccato promissione vitae aeternae excidisset, inde patet quod sub illo foedere, nullus erat locus veniae & remissionis, cujus promissiones Evangelico foe-deri propriae sunt. Neque lex praecise sumpta, & ut Evangelio & gratiae opponitur, locum dabat poenitentiae, absque qua peccatum omne vita coelesti in aeternum exclu-dit.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, God, striking a legal covenant with integral man, exacted from him obedience everywhere perfect and absolute in all its numbers, as a condition without which he could not attain eternal and blessed life and escape the divine curse. But that perfection which the law in its rigor, and as it was first given to man, requires, excludes every sin, even the lightest. And therefore by any sin even the lightest, integral man could fall from eternal life and incur the divine curse. Whence it manifestly follows that every sin, however light, is by its nature mortal, not venial. But that under the legal covenant integral man by any sin would have fallen from the promise of eternal life is thence plain: that under that covenant there was no place for pardon and remission, whose promises are proper to the evangelical covenant. Nor did the law precisely taken, and as opposed to the Gospel and grace, give place to repentance, without which every sin forever excludes from heavenly life.
pass_b_english: Legal covenant with upright Adam: life only by number-perfect obedience—any lightest fault lost life and drew the curse.
No pardon-lane under law-alone; repentance and remission belong to the gospel covenant—so every sin is mortal by nature.
